issues.description: The problem statement requires that the save(..) helper in PersonService "must be a protected helper method" and instructs students to call this method from addParent/addChild/removeParent/removeChild. However, both the template and the solution provide save(..) as a public method (template: public Person save(Person person); solution: public Person save(Person person);). This is a visibility mismatch: if students followed the problem text and changed save to protected, PersonResource (in package de.tum.in.ase.eist.rest) could no longer call save(...) (protected only grants access to subclasses and package members), which would break controller code and tests. Conversely, the template and tests assume save is public. This contradiction can confuse students about the intended visibility and how controllers/tests should interact with PersonService.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the artifacts consistent. Recommended: update the problem statement to not require save(..) to be protected — instead state that students should use the provided save(..) helper (which is public in the template) to persist changes, or explicitly state that save(...) remains public so controllers and tests can call it. Alternatively (less recommended), change the template/solution to alter how controllers persist entities (so save can be made non-public) and update tests accordingly, but this would be a larger structural change.
